item.title: [LINGUIST List — Conference Announcements] Confs: 45th West Coast Conference on Formal Linguistics
item.description: The West Coast Conference on Formal Linguistics, or WCCFL (pronounced /ˈwɪkfəl/), occurs annually in the spring at a university in western North America. WCCFL 45 returns to Salt Lake City, hosted by the Department of Linguistics of the University of Utah. We invite abstracts for 20-minute talks and posters on any theoretical or formal aspect of natural language, including but not limited to phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, and their interfaces. item.title: [LINGUIST List — Conference Announcements] Confs: 12th All India Conference of Linguistics and Folklore
item.description: The conference aims to explore folklore as a linguistic and interdisciplinary domain, examining its role in preserving multilingual heritage, transmitting traditional knowledge and enriching Indian Knowledge Systems. It also seeks to engage with contemporary developments in mother-tongue education, digital humanities, language documentation and artificial intelligence. item.title: [LINGUIST List — Conference Announcements] Confs: Purdue Linguistics Symposium 2027
item.description: The Department of Linguistics at Purdue University is announcing its annual Purdue Linguistics Symposium (PLS) 2027. We invite scholars working within all theoretical and applied areas of linguistics to submit their research and join us at PLS 2027. Topics include, but are not limited to syntax, semantics, syntax-semantics interface, phonetics, phonology, morphology, L2 acquisition, bilingualism, pragmatics, historical linguistics, sociolinguistics, sign language, and corpus linguistics. item.title: [LINGUIST List — Calls for Papers] Calls: Journal of Arabic Sociolinguistics (Jrnl)
item.description: The Journal of Arabic Sociolinguistics welcomes research which applies new theories and methodologies to Arabic data. We are particularly interested in articles that address the relation between linguistic variation and identity, variation and sociolinguistic variables (including but not limited to location, social class, education, age, gender, and urbanization), and variation and political contexts . item.title: [LINGUIST List — Calls for Papers] Calls: Caucasus Survey - "Special Issue: Changing Linguistic Ecologies in the Caucasus" (Jrnl)
item.description: The Caucasus is characterized by extraordinary linguistic diversity and a long history of multilingualism, language contact, and cultural interaction. Across the region, however, linguistic ecologies are undergoing significant transformations in response to changing demographic patterns, migration, urbanization, educational policies, political developments, conflict, and globalization.
